newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine winter sowing over,'97 harvest may rebound.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine winter sowing over,'97 harvest may rebound.

text.p: Ukraine's all-important winter grain sowing campaign is complete, and with good weather conditions, the former Soviet republic's harvest could rebound next year from this year's disaster, industry officials said on Thursday.
Valentyn Tymoshenko, deputy head of the ministry's crop department, told Reuters up to 90 percent of winter grain was in considerably better condition than at this time last year.
Volodymyr Krut, a deputy chairman of the Agricultural Science Academy, said soil in nearly all areas had enough moisture.
"If we have a favourable winter, Ukraine may be able to boost next year's grain harvest to up to 35 million tonnes -- the same level as in 1995 -- or maybe even more," Krut said.
Much of Ukraine's grain harvest consists of winter wheat.
Officials are hoping for a mild winter, but with plenty of snow cover in the event of frosts. Temperatures all over the country have been mild so far this winter.

Winter wheat was sown on 7.44 million hectares out of a total of 8.24 million sown to winter grain, compared to 7.89 million hectares last year. Government plans called for sowing 8.61 million hectares with winter grain.
Agriculture Minister Anatoly Horishko last month predicted the 1997 grain harvest at 36 million tonnes.
Tymoshenko said that although the 1996 harvest campaign was finished, there was no final figure yet for this year's crop.
The grain harvest this year has been forecast at a poor 26 million tonnes, far below last year's 36.5 million. Government officials blamed severe drought at the beginning of the summer.
Winter wheat accounted for 13.18 million tonnes of this year's harvest against 16.4 million tonnes last year.
According to Agriculture Ministry data, the Ukrainian state sector harvested 1.08 million tonnes of maize this autumn in addition to 21.60 million tonnes of other grains.
Government officials said the small private farm sector had also harvested up to three million tonnes of grain.

Ukraine also planned to double fertiliser use from this year's level to try to increase next year's harvest, Tymoshenko added. But Krut said the farm sector's main problem was lack of money, which could hit government plans to significantly increase fertiliser production. --Kiev Newsroom, +380 44 229 2264
